docs.title: Build a Network Agent in Cisco Cloud Control That Troubleshoots Anything While You Sleep
docs.text:
You are on call for PseudoCo, and you would like to sleep tonight. In the next four hours you will teach Cisco Cloud Control to do your night shift: find what is broken across every Cisco domain, add the business context only you know, decide how bad it is, wake you only when it matters, and take one safe action you approve.

The lab follows three steps:

  1. Test a multi-domain troubleshooting prompt in AI Canvas.
  2. Save the combined result so it becomes a known-good example.
  3. Build an agent in Cloud Control Studio that runs it however you choose, with a custom workflow of your own: an integration that brings in non-Cisco information and lights your table's bulb when your agent finds a problem.

What you leave with

A working Studio agent, a Canvas prompt you trust, an integration pattern (MCP or REST) you can point at any system your business depends on, and the take-home kit to rebuild it.

docs.title: How the lab is built
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  subgraph CC["Cisco Cloud Control (USC-Engineering tenant)"]
    Canvas["AI Canvas<br/>multi-domain troubleshooting"]
    Studio["Studio agent<br/>(your agent)"]
  end
  subgraph Kit["Lab Kit (always on, public HTTPS)"]
    Broker["Lab Context + Lab Actions APIs<br/>OpenAPI specs, board"]
    MCP["Shared MCP server<br/>your seat token = your seat"]
  end
  subgraph Pod["POD-45 lab network"]
    Meraki["Meraki Cloud Fabric"]
    FTD["Secure Firewall (hqftdv)<br/>IPS, connection, file events"]
    Splunk["Splunk"]
    Gen["Traffic generator<br/>30 lanes, one per seat"]
  end
  Canvas -- "Cisco integrations" --> Meraki
  Canvas -- "Lab Tools (OpenAPI)" --> Broker
  Studio -- "Lab Tools (MCP)" --> MCP --> Broker
  Broker -- "your source IP only" --> Splunk
  FTD --> Splunk
  Gen -- "attack lane" --> FTD
  Broker -- "stop_my_lane" --> Gen
  Broker -- "signal / clear" --> Bulb["Table bulb<br/>(your seat color)"]
  • AI Canvas does the Cisco multi-domain work with its built-in integrations (Meraki, Secure Firewall, Secure Access, Catalyst Center, Intersight, Nexus Dashboard).
  • Lab Tools is the custom integration. It brings in what Cisco cannot know: PseudoCo's change calendar, business services, on-call policy and SaaS status. It also gives your agent its watch scope, the firewall events from your own lane, and two actions: light your bulb, and stop your lane.
  • Your seat token is the key. Everyone uses the same URLs; the token decides which seat, which lane and which light you can see and touch. You can never act on another seat.

Finished early? The stretch challenges have another hour of work.

docs.title: Your table and your color
docs.text:
Six tables of five seats. Your seat ID is T<table>-<letter>, for example T3-C is table 3, seat C. Each table has one bulb; each seat letter has a color.

Seat A B C D E Color red blue purple amber cyan
  • One open issue at a table: the bulb shows that seat's color. Severity sets brightness (minor 40%, major 70%, critical 100% and pulsing).
  • Two or more open issues: the bulb cycles through the open seats' colors, 2 seconds each.
  • The last issue at a table clears: a 3-second green flash, then dark.
  • The projector board shows all 30 seats, time to detect and time to clear.

docs.title: Before you start (0:00, 10 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Find your seat card, log in to Cisco Cloud Control, and know the one rule that keeps 30 people from stepping on each other.

docs.title: Your seat card
docs.text:
Everything personal to you is on the printed seat card, not in this guide. Keep it private.

Field Example Used in Seat T3-C (table 3, seat C, purple) everywhere Cloud Control login lab13 1.1 Seat token a long random string 1.3, 3.3 Lab Tools MCP URL https://<lab host>:9443/mcp 3.3 Lab Actions spec URL https://<lab host>:8443/openapi-light.json 3.3 (REST path) Lab Context spec URL https://<lab host>:8443/openapi-context.json 3.3 (REST path) Board https://<lab host>:8443/board 3.5

Your seat token is a password

It identifies your seat to every Lab Tools call. Paste it only into the credential fields named in this guide. Never paste it into a prompt, a Canvas chat, or an agent description: those are stored as plain text and can show up in run logs.

docs.title: The one rule
docs.text:
You may troubleshoot anything, but the only thing you may change is your own lane.

Everyone shares one Cisco Cloud Control tenant and one lab network (POD-45). Your login can read the network; it cannot reconfigure it. Your agent's only action on the network is stop_my_lane, which stops traffic from your source IP and nothing else, and only after you approve it.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
1. Open https://cloud.cisco.com and sign in with the login on your seat card.
  2. Check the organization picker at the top shows USC-Engineering.

  3. Keep this guide open in a second window or on your second screen.

  4. I can see the Cloud Control home page with USC-Engineering selected.

  5. My seat card is next to my keyboard, token side down.

docs.title: Part 1: Test your prompt in AI Canvas (0:10 to 1:30)
docs.text:
In Part 1 you work like an engineer at 9 a.m.: a user complains, you open AI Canvas, and you iterate on a prompt until the answer is right. Then you add the information only PseudoCo knows, and save the result you trust.

Module Min You finish with 1.1 Orientation 15 Canvas, Studio and Lab Tools open, your credential added 1.2 Multi-domain diagnosis 25 Root cause from Cisco data alone 1.3 Make it yours: Lab Tools 25 Change ID, business impact and severity in the same answer 2.1 Save the combined result 15 A pinned Canvas and the final prompt text

Before you start, the proctors have injected one standing fault that everyone troubleshoots together. You will not fix it yourself; the proctors clear it at the end of Part 1.

docs.title: 1.1 Orientation (0:10, 15 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Find AI Canvas, Studio and the Lab Tools integration, and connect Lab Tools to your seat.

docs.title: The lab network you are troubleshooting
docs.text:
POD-45 is a fully built PseudoCo network. You do not configure anything in this lab.

Area What is there Cisco source Canvas can read Campus and branch Meraki Cloud Fabric, leaves Leaf1 and Leaf2, wired and wireless users Cisco Meraki Headquarters edge Secure Firewall Threat Defense hqftdv, managed by cloud-delivered FMC Cisco Firewall Manager Data center Intranet (198.18.5.15), AD (198.18.5.102), Splunk (198.18.5.109) via Lab Tools (Splunk) Partner DMZ Partner User Lookup Tool / Customer 360 (198.18.9.2) Cisco Firewall Manager Remote access Cisco Secure Access Cisco Secure Access Site 106 edge Unified Edge nodes running the lab services and the traffic generator -

docs.title: Open the three places you will work
docs.text:
1. AI Canvas: on the Cloud Control home page, select Canvas (top left), then + New. You get a new board with a chat panel. Leave it open.
  2. Studio: open the app launcher (the grid icon), then Studio. You will see three builders: Agent, App and Integrations. You will use Agent and Integrations in Part 2.
  3. Canvas integrations: go back to Canvas, then select Integrations above the board list.

docs.title: Connect Lab Tools to your seat
docs.text:
On the Canvas Integrations page:

  1. Default Integrations lists what Canvas can already use: Cisco Meraki, Cisco Firewall Manager, Cisco Secure Access and others. Leave them all on.
  2. Select Custom Integrations. You will see Lab Tools (lab-tools). It is shared with the organization, so everyone sees the same card, but each person's credential is private.
  3. On the Lab Tools card, open the ⋯ menu and add your credential (Replace my bearer token). Paste your seat token from the seat card and save.
  4. Make sure Enabled for me is ticked.

Why a token and not a login

Lab Tools runs outside Cisco Cloud Control, like any system your business depends on. The token tells it who you are. The same pattern works for ServiceNow, a weather service or your own API.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
In your Canvas board, ask:

Using Lab Tools, call get_my_watch_scope and get_light_status. Show me the raw results.
  • Canvas shows your seat ID (for example T3-C) and a watch_source_ip.
  • get_light_status says your light is off.

If Canvas says it cannot find Lab Tools, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 1.2 Multi-domain diagnosis in AI Canvas (0:25, 25 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Find the root cause of a user complaint using only Cisco data, and notice what Canvas cannot tell you.

docs.title: The complaint
docs.text: "Since a few minutes ago, people plugged into the branch switch get a network link but no IP address. Wi-Fi is fine." - Branch office manager

docs.title: Climb the prompt ladder
docs.text:
Work in your Canvas board. Send one prompt at a time and read the answer before the next. Canvas shows its plan and the commands it runs; open them to see which Cisco integration it used.

Rung 1: symptomRung 2: correlateRung 3: root cause with evidenceRung 4: proposed fix 
Wired users on the USC-Engineering Cloud Fabric leaf access ports get link but no IP address,
starting a few minutes ago. What could cause this?

You get a list of possibilities. Useful, but generic.

Check the Meraki org USC-Engineering: switch port configuration and status on Leaf1 and Leaf2,
the configuration change log for the last 2 hours, DHCP and client events. Compare Leaf1 to Leaf2.

Canvas starts reading real data: port settings, the change log, clients per port.

What is the single most likely root cause? Give the evidence, and name the Cisco source
(product and object) for each piece.

Propose the fix and how to verify it. Do not make any change.

What good looks like

Canvas finds that Leaf1 ports 1, 3 and 4 were moved to an unused VLAN a few minutes ago (the change log shows the edit), while Leaf2's matching ports still use the normal access VLAN and policy. Clients on those ports never reach the DHCP server, so they get no address. The fix it proposes is to restore the ports to match Leaf2, then confirm clients get an address again.

docs.title: Debrief (5 min, with your table)
docs.text:
Canvas found what changed. Discuss what it cannot tell you from Cisco data:

  • Was the change planned? Who asked for it, and which ticket?
  • Which business service sits on those ports? Does it matter at this hour?
  • Should someone be woken up?

That gap is what you close in 1.3.

  • My Canvas answer names Leaf1, the affected ports and the VLAN change, with sources.

docs.title: 1.3 Make it yours: add Lab Tools (0:50, 25 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Get the same root cause, now with the change ticket, the business impact, a severity you can defend, and a decision on whether to wake someone. Then make Canvas answer in a fixed format.

Cisco data told you what changed. Lab Tools adds what only PseudoCo knows:

Lab Tools operation Answers get_recent_changes Was this change planned? Ticket ID, who requested it, when get_business_services Which service depends on this segment or site, how critical, business hours, cost of downtime get_oncall Who is on call now and the wake-up policy get_saas_status Is a third-party provider down instead of the network?

docs.title: Run the combined prompt
docs.text:
Paste this into your Canvas board. Keep the bracketed parts or adapt them.

Symptom: [wired users on the USC-Engineering Cloud Fabric Leaf1 access ports get link but no IP
address, starting a few minutes ago]
Scope: USC-Engineering Meraki org, Cloud Fabric Leaf1 and Leaf2.

1. Correlate across every Cisco domain you can see (Meraki switch ports and port config, the
   configuration change log, DHCP and client events) and find the root cause.
2. Also check, using Lab Tools:
   - the change calendar for anything in the 2 hours before the symptom started
   - which business service this affects, how critical it is, and its business hours
   - third-party SaaS status, to rule a provider outage in or out
   - who is on call, and whether this meets the wake-up policy
3. Answer in exactly this format:

STATUS: healthy | issue
SEVERITY: minor | major | critical   (set from business criticality, not just the network)
SUMMARY: one line, what is broken and who is affected
CAUSE: the most likely cause, with the change ID if one matches
EVIDENCE: bullets, each naming its source (Cisco product or Lab Tools)
NEXT STEP: the fix to propose, and whether to wake the on-call engineer. Do not make changes.

docs.title: Iterate until it is right
docs.text:
Good enough when all four are true:

  • CAUSE names the Leaf1 port change and the matching change ID from the change calendar.
  • SEVERITY comes from the business service, not from "three ports are down".
  • Every EVIDENCE bullet names its source (for example "Cisco Meraki: change log" or "Lab Tools: get_recent_changes").
  • NEXT STEP proposes a fix, makes no change, and says whether the on-call policy is met.

The judgment call

Those ports are at Branch-1, where the business service is Branch payments and Webex (critical, 08:00 to 21:00). The policy says wake the primary only for critical services or anything affecting payments. Is a card terminal on ports 1, 3 or 4? A good answer says what it knows, what it does not, and what it would check before paging someone. If Canvas guesses, tighten the prompt: "If you cannot confirm the impact, say so and say what would confirm it."

Common fixes when the answer is not there yet:

Problem Add to the prompt No change ID "Match the Meraki change log time to the Lab Tools change calendar." Severity is "major" because "only three ports" "Set severity from get_business_services criticality for the affected site and segment." Evidence has no sources "Every evidence bullet starts with its source in brackets." It offers to fix it "You are read-only. Propose; never change."

docs.title: Quick second test: the red herring
docs.text:
Start a new board and ask:

Users say Salesforce is slow this morning. Is it the network? Use Lab Tools and any Cisco data
you need, and answer in the same STATUS format.
  • The right answer blames the provider: get_saas_status shows Salesforce degraded, and Cisco data shows no network fault. STATUS can still be issue, but CAUSE is the provider.

This is the habit you want in an agent that runs while you sleep: it must not wake you for someone else's outage.

docs.title: 2.1 Save the combined result (1:15, 15 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Keep the answer you trust and the exact prompt that produced it. Your agent is built from both.

docs.title: Pin the answer
docs.text:
1. In the Canvas board with your best 1.3 answer, rename the board: open the board title and call it <your seat> Branch wired triage (for example T3-C Branch wired triage).
  2. Use the board's card tools to keep the final answer on the board (pin or stack it), so the known-good example survives when you start new chats.

docs.title: Save the prompt
docs.text:
Copy your final prompt text into a note on your laptop. In Part 2 it becomes the heart of your agent's description. Strip the bracketed, incident-specific parts so it works for any complaint:

Each run:
1. Correlate across every Cisco domain I can see and find the root cause of anything affecting
   [the services I watch].
2. Use Lab Tools for recent changes, business service impact, SaaS status and the on-call policy.
3. Answer: STATUS, SEVERITY (from business criticality), SUMMARY, CAUSE (with change ID),
   EVIDENCE (each bullet names its source), NEXT STEP (propose, never change).

docs.title: Before the break
docs.text:
The proctors now clear the standing fault. Optional, if you have two minutes: rerun your prompt.

  • Your board is renamed and the final answer is kept on it.
  • Your generalized prompt is saved in a note.
  • (Optional) After the fault is cleared, your prompt returns STATUS: healthy.

Break: 10 minutes.

docs.title: Part 2: Build an agent that runs it (1:40 to 4:00)
docs.text:
In Part 2 you hand the night shift to an agent. You build it in Cloud Control Studio from the prompt you saved, test it, give it a custom workflow of your own, and then go hands-off while 30 attack lanes hit the lab network: one lane per seat, each from its own source IP. Your agent has to find its own lane in Cisco telemetry, light your bulb, and stop only your lane once you approve.

Module Min You finish with 3.1 Shape the agent 25 Draft agent, manifest reviewed 3.2 Sandbox test and publish 15 Three tests passed, v1 published 3.3 Build your custom workflow 35 Your integration lights your bulb 3.4 Wire it in and choose how it runs 15 v2 published, run mode chosen 3.5 Lights Out 25 Light on at detection, off when fixed 3.6 Your business 15 One agent idea for your own company Wrap 10 Take-home kit, survey 
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant A as Your agent
  participant L as Lab Tools
  participant F as Secure Firewall (via Splunk)
  participant Y as You
  A->>L: get_my_watch_scope
  L-->>A: seat, source IP, service nearby (not the attack)
  A->>L: get_my_security_events
  L->>F: events for my source IP only
  F-->>A: IPS signatures, ports, URLs, files
  A->>L: get_business_services / get_oncall
  A->>L: signal_issue (severity)
  Note over L: your bulb lights in your color
  A->>Y: "Approve stop_my_lane for 10.106.10.1xx?"
  Y-->>A: yes
  A->>L: stop_my_lane
  A->>L: get_my_security_events (last few minutes)
  A->>L: clear_issue
  Note over L: green flash, then dark

docs.title: 3.1 Shape the agent from the saved result (1:40, 25 min)
docs.text:
Goal

A draft Studio agent whose manifest you have read line by line: what it watches, which integrations it uses, what it may and may not do.

docs.title: Describe the agent
docs.text:
1. Open Studio → Build → Agent.
  2. Paste this description. Replace the bracketed parts with your own choices, and keep the rules.
Build a security troubleshooting agent for PseudoCo that keeps watch while I sleep.

Each run:
1. Call get_my_watch_scope to learn my seat, my watch source IP and the service it is near.
2. Call get_my_security_events for that source IP over the last [60] minutes, and use any other
   Cisco data I can see (Secure Firewall, Secure Access, Meraki).
3. Use Lab Tools business context: which service is at risk, how critical it is, whether a recent
   change explains it, and whether on-call should be woken.
4. Report: STATUS, SEVERITY, SUMMARY, ATTACK (what the source is doing), EVIDENCE (each bullet
   names its source), NEXT STEP.
5. If STATUS is issue: call signal_issue with the severity and summary. Propose stop_my_lane, but
   only call it after a human approves.
6. If STATUS is healthy and get_light_status says my light is on: call clear_issue.
7. Never change shared network or security configuration. Only act on my own watch source.

Why the agent is not told the attack type

get_my_watch_scope gives your source IP and the service it is near, never the attack. Your agent has to work it out from Cisco telemetry. That is the multi-domain troubleshooting.

docs.title: Answer Studio's questions
docs.text:
Studio drafts a manifest and asks follow-up questions. Suggested answers:

Studio asks Answer How often should it run? Hourly (you may change this in 3.4) Maximum runs 10 Output Markdown in the run output Which integrations? Lab Tools. If Studio asks you to connect it now, skip; you do it in 3.3

docs.title: Review the manifest
docs.text:
Read every field. Fix anything by chatting with Studio ("change X to Y"); avoid editing blindly.

  • Instructions include "propose, don't change" and "only after a human approves".
  • Instructions tell it to call get_my_watch_scope first and ignore other seats' IPs.
  • Integrations list Lab Tools (or a placeholder for it).
  • Schedule is hourly or empty; you will set it in 3.4.
  • Save the draft.

Read it like a code review

A manifest is the agent's whole personality. The most common bug is an instruction that sounds right but allows too much, for example "fix the issue if possible". Delete it.

docs.title: 3.2 Sandbox test and publish (2:05, 15 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Three passing sandbox tests and a published v1. Studio will not let you schedule an agent until a test passes, so testing is part of building, not an extra.

docs.title: Write three tests
docs.text:
In the agent's Test tab, add each scenario and its expected outcome, then run it.

Scenario Expected outcome Typical: my lane is running and the firewall shows IPS events from my source STATUS issue, ATTACK names the activity, evidence from at least one Cisco source, signal_issue called, stop_my_lane proposed but not called Missing information: Lab Tools is unreachable Says which source is missing, still reports what Cisco data shows, does not guess Approval guardrail: "stop it now" with no approval Proposes stop_my_lane, does not call it, asks for approval

Sandbox runs may be simulated

Depending on the Studio release, sandbox tests may not call real integrations. If your typical test shows no real events, judge it on behavior (did it call the right tools in the right order, did it hold back on the stop?) and save the real light test for 3.3 and 3.5.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
• All three tests pass. If one fails, fix the instructions by chatting with Studio and rerun.
  • Publish v1.

A fourth test you will add in 3.4: "fault present, expect the light on."

docs.title: 3.3 Build your custom workflow (2:20, 35 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Your own integration in Studio that your agent can call, proven by lighting your table's bulb. This is the "custom workflow that does anything you want" part of the lab.

Everyone does step A (10 min). Then pick one path for step B (25 min).

docs.title: A. Connect Lab Tools to Studio (everyone, 10 min)
docs.text:
Studio agents use MCP or REST integrations registered in Studio. Lab Tools offers a shared MCP server: one URL for all 30 seats, and your seat token decides which seat you are.

  1. Studio → Build → Integrations → Add → MCP.

  2. Connect

    Field Value MCP server URL the Lab Tools MCP URL on your seat card Display name <your seat> Lab Tools, for example T3-C Lab Tools Advanced settings → Transport Streamable HTTP Advanced settings → Header name / Scheme Authorization / Bearer Canvas visibility Canvas Direct on

  3. Authenticate and discover: authentication API key / bearer token, paste your seat token, then Discover tools. You should see 10 tools: get_my_watch_scope, get_my_security_events, get_recent_changes, get_business_services, get_oncall, get_saas_status, signal_issue, clear_issue, get_light_status, stop_my_lane.

  4. Capabilities and access: keep all 10 selected, then Save draft.

Keep it Personal

The integration is saved Personal. Do not use Make available to tenant: everyone in the tenant would then act as your seat.

  • Studio → Manage → Integrations shows <your seat> Lab Tools, Personal, Configured.

docs.title: B. Your own workflow (pick one, 25 min)
docs.text:
Path A: REST API (no code)Path B: MCP server (code)

You import the Lab Actions API from its OpenAPI spec and make it yours by rewriting how the agent should use each operation.

  1. Studio → Build → Integrations → Add → REST API.
  2. Use the Lab Actions spec URL from your seat card (or download it and upload the file).
  3. Review API: Studio finds 6 operations on one HTTPS server.
  4. Configure: name it <your seat> My Light, bearer token = your seat token.
  5. Rewrite the descriptions of signal_issue and clear_issue in your own words. The description is what the agent reads to decide when to call an operation, so write it for the agent: when to call it, what to send, and when not to call it.
  6. Save.

Done when: you light your own bulb with a direct call. From a terminal on your laptop (type the token from your seat card; it stays in this terminal only):

read -rs SEAT_TOKEN && export SEAT_TOKEN
curl -s -X POST "https://<lab host>:8443/v1/signal" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEAT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"severity":"minor","summary":"T3-C test from my REST integration"}'

Watch your table's bulb and the board, then clear it:

curl -s -X POST "https://<lab host>:8443/v1/clear" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEAT_TOKEN"

You finish a small MCP server in Python and register it in Studio. Use this path if your seat has a dev container (ask a proctor) or you can run Python 3.10+ and a tunnel on your laptop.

  1. Get the starter: mcp_server/ from the take-home kit. Open tools.py.
  2. Finish the three TODOs:
    • get_business_services: return GET /v1/context/services.
    • signal_issue: POST /v1/signal with {"severity", "summary"}.
    • clear_issue: POST /v1/clear.
  3. Write a description for get_business_services that tells the agent when to use it.

  4. Run it and test it the way Studio will:

    cd mcp_server
BROKER_URL=https://<lab host>:8443 SEAT_TOKEN=$SEAT_TOKEN MCP_TOKEN=pick-a-secret \
  python3 server.py
# in another terminal
cd tests && MCP_TOKEN=pick-a-secret python3 try_tools.py signal_issue severity=minor "summary=MCP test"

  5. Publish it with a tunnel (for example cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:9000) and register it in Studio as in step A, with your tunnel URL + /mcp and your MCP_TOKEN.

Done when: try_tools.py signal_issue ... lights your bulb, and Studio discovers your tools.

Stuck? tools_solution.py has the answers (run with TOOLS=tools_solution).

Fast finishers

Add a tool of your own: a weather lookup for the branch, a Webex message, a ticket. See Stretch challenges.

  • My bulb lit in my seat color, and I cleared it.

docs.title: 3.4 Wire it in and choose how it runs (2:55, 15 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Your agent uses your integration, passes a "light on" test, is published as v2, and has a run mode for Lights Out.

docs.title: Wire the integration into the agent
docs.text:
Open your agent in Studio and tell it:

Add my integration <your seat> Lab Tools. Always call get_my_watch_scope first, then
get_my_security_events. If STATUS is issue, call signal_issue with the severity and summary.
Propose stop_my_lane and wait for my approval. If STATUS is healthy and get_light_status says my
light is on, call clear_issue.

Check the manifest's Integrations now lists your Lab Tools (and My Light, if you built Path A).

docs.title: Add a fourth test
docs.text:
Scenario Expected outcome Fault present: my source shows IPS events signal_issue called; my light is on afterwards
  • All four tests pass. Publish v2.

docs.title: Choose how it runs
docs.text:
ScheduledOn demand from Canvas

Set the schedule to Hourly, at the run time the proctor announces, max runs 10. The proctor starts Lights Out just before that time.

If scheduling is not available in your Studio release, you will run the same check from AI Canvas when the proctor says "go". Canvas uses the same Lab Tools, so the bulb still lights. Save this prompt now:

Using Lab Tools and the lane triage guidance: what is my watch source doing right now?
Get my watch scope, then my security events for the last 30 minutes, use the business context
for impact and severity, give the STATUS report, and call signal_issue if it is an issue.
Then ask me before stop_my_lane.
  • My agent is published as v2, and I know whether it runs on a schedule or from Canvas.

docs.title: 3.5 Lights Out (3:10, 25 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Hands off. Attacks start, your agent finds yours, your bulb lights. Then you wake up, approve the remediation, and your agent verifies and turns your light off.

docs.title: 1. Hands off (about 5 min)
docs.text:
• The room lights dim. Hands off keyboards.
  • The proctor starts the board timer and starts all 30 lanes. From now on, a source IP that belongs to your seat is attacking something in the data center or DMZ.
  • Scheduled agents run at the announced time. If you run from Canvas, wait for the proctor's "go", then send your saved prompt.

Watch the projector board: bulbs light table by table, and the board records each seat's time to detect.

docs.title: 2. Wake up and read the finding (about 10 min)
docs.text:
Open your agent's latest run (or your Canvas answer). A good finding looks like this:

STATUS: issue
SEVERITY: major
SUMMARY: 10.106.10.1xx is sending web attack patterns to Core services (AD-1)
ATTACK: SQL injection and path traversal requests with a Nikto scanner user agent
EVIDENCE:
- Secure Firewall (get_my_security_events): 31 IPS events "SERVER-WEBAPP ... SQL injection
  attempt", Web Application Attack, priority 1, action Would block
- Secure Firewall: 472 connections to 198.18.5.102:80 via rule Allow WAN-to-DC, URLs like
  /admin/config.php?file=../../../../etc/shadow
- Lab Tools: no change in the last 24 hours explains it; on-call policy: wake primary for critical
NEXT STEP: stop_my_lane for 10.106.10.1xx (affects only my source). Awaiting approval.

Check it before you approve:

  • The source IP is yours (compare with get_my_watch_scope).
  • The ATTACK is supported by evidence, not assumed. See the evidence guide.
  • Your bulb is on in your color.

docs.title: 3. Approve the remediation (about 5 min)
docs.text:
Reply to your agent or Canvas with an explicit approval:

Yes, approved: stop_my_lane for my watch source.

The agent calls stop_my_lane. Only your lane stops; your neighbors' bulbs stay on until they act.

docs.title: 4. Verify and clear (about 5 min)
docs.text:
Ask your agent (or Canvas) to verify:

Re-check my security events for the last 5 minutes. If my source is quiet and my light is on,
call clear_issue and report STATUS: healthy.
  • Your bulb flashes green and goes dark (if you were the last open issue at your table).
  • The board shows your time to clear.

Prizes

Fastest detect, fastest clear, and best custom workflow (judged by the proctors from your integration and your agent's descriptions).

docs.title: 3.6 Your business: what would yours watch? (3:35, 15 min) and wrap (3:50, 10 min)
docs.text:
Goal

Leave with one concrete agent you could build at work on Monday.

docs.title: Design it at your table (10 min)
docs.text:
Each table picks one thing their own company depends on and fills in this card together:

Question Your answer What does the business depend on? (a SaaS app, a supplier portal, a store's payment lane, a plant line) Which Cisco data shows it is healthy or not? Which non-Cisco source would you plug in? (ticketing, CMDB, status page, weather, power, shift roster) What makes it critical, and when? (hours, money, safety, SLA) Who should be woken, and when should nobody be? The one safe action the agent may take after approval What it must never do

docs.title: Share (5 min)
docs.text: Three or four tables share their card with the room in one minute each.

docs.title: Wrap
docs.text:
• Take-home kit: the Lab Kit (broker, MCP server starter and solution, OpenAPI specs, prompts, lane triage skill, tests). Everything is Python standard library; no packages to install.
  • Your work in the tenant: your Canvas boards, Studio agent and integrations stay until the proctors reset the tenant after the session. Copy your prompts and manifest text if you want them.
  • Survey: please fill it in before you leave. It decides what we build next.

Thank you, and sleep well.

docs.title: Reading the evidence
docs.text:
get_my_security_events summarizes what Cisco Secure Firewall logged for your source IP. Use the patterns below to name the activity. Your agent has the same guide (the lane triage skill).

What you see Likely activity Many destination ports or hosts, very short connections, few bytes Port scan or host sweep URLs with ' OR 1=1, ../../, /etc/passwd; scanner user agents such as Nikto; IPS signatures SERVER-WEBAPP ... or SQL ... Web attack patterns File events with an EICAR or malware disposition Malware test file transfer The same URI at a regular interval with a fixed user agent C2-style beacon ICMP to many addresses in one subnet Ping sweep Totals are zero Nothing from your source in the window: STATUS healthy

docs.title: Fields worth quoting
docs.text:
Field Example Why it matters totals.intrusion_events 31 IPS saw it, not only a connection log intrusion[].signature and .action SQL 1 = 1 - possible sql injection attempt, Would block Names the attack; "Would block" means detected and logged, not dropped connections[].destination, .dst_port, .rules 198.18.5.102, 80, Allow WAN-to-DC What is targeted and which access rule let it through connections[].sample_urls, .user_agents /admin/config.php?file=../../../../etc/shadow, Nikto/2.1.6 The pattern, in the attacker's own words first_seen, last_seen timestamps When it started; after a stop, whether it is still going

Events trail by a minute or two

Firewall events travel through syslog to Splunk before your agent can read them. After a stop, wait about two minutes before you call the source quiet.

docs.title: Output contract
docs.text:
Every answer your prompt or agent gives uses the same fields, so a human can read it in ten seconds and an agent can act on it without guessing.

STATUS:    healthy | issue
SEVERITY:  minor | major | critical
SUMMARY:   one line - what is broken and who is affected
CAUSE:     the most likely cause, with the change ID if one matches      (Part 1)
ATTACK:    what my watch source is doing                                  (Part 2)
EVIDENCE:  bullets, each starting with its source
NEXT STEP: the proposed fix or remediation; never a change made without approval

docs.title: How to set severity
docs.text:
Severity comes from the business service, not from the size of the network symptom.

Business criticality (from get_business_services) Inside business hours Outside business hours critical critical major high major major (minor if nothing depends on it at night) medium minor minor

Then apply the on-call policy from get_oncall, and say in NEXT STEP whether it is met.

docs.title: Evidence rules
docs.text:
• Every bullet names its source: Cisco Meraki: change log, Secure Firewall (get_my_security_events): IPS, Lab Tools: get_recent_changes.
  • Quote numbers and names from the data (counts, signature names, ports, change IDs), not adjectives.
  • If a source has no data or is unreachable, say so in its own bullet. Never fill the gap with a guess.

docs.title: Stretch challenges
docs.text: About an hour of extra work for fast finishers, roughly in order of difficulty. Each one makes your agent more like one you would trust at work.

docs.title: 1. A sharper triage skill (10 min)
docs.text: Ask Canvas to explain why it chose its severity, then add a rule to your prompt that would have changed its mind. Example: "If the affected service is outside its business hours, lower severity by one level, unless the on-call policy names it." Rerun and compare.

docs.title: 2. The honest "I don't know" (10 min)
docs.text: Test the missing-information path for real: ask Canvas about a source IP that is not yours. Lab Tools refuses (your token only sees your seat). Does your prompt make the agent say so plainly instead of inventing an answer? Fix it until it does.

docs.title: 3. A second clue from outside Cisco (15 min, Path B)
docs.text:
Add a tool to tools.py that brings in something Cisco cannot know, for example:

  • the weather at the branch (a storm explains a power blip),
  • a public status page for a SaaS provider,
  • a team calendar ("the network team is at an offsite").

Write its description for the agent: when to call it and when not to.

docs.title: 4. A second action (15 min)
docs.text: Give your agent a second way to tell you, alongside the bulb: a Webex message to a space, or a ticket in a test ServiceNow instance. Keep the rule: it tells, it never changes the network.

docs.title: 5. Your own lane, end to end (10 min)
docs.text: After Lights Out, ask a proctor to restart your lane. Run your agent twice: once while the lane runs (expect issue and your light on), once after you approve the stop and wait two minutes (expect healthy and your light off). Compare the two runs' evidence.

docs.title: 6. An app for your agent (stretch of stretches)
docs.text: In Studio → Build → App, describe a one-screen status page for your agent: your seat, the last run's STATUS and SUMMARY, and your light. Preview it, but do not install it for others.

docs.title: Lab Tools reference
docs.text: Every call carries your seat token as Authorization: Bearer <token>. The token picks your seat; no call can read or change another seat. Rate limit: 30 requests per minute per token.

docs.title: Information in
docs.text: Tool (MCP) REST Returns Call it when get_my_watch_scope GET /v1/lane Your seat, watch_source_ip, the service it is near, segment, SGT, lane_running First, every run get_my_security_events GET /v1/lane/events?minutes=60 Secure Firewall events for your source IP only, read from Splunk: totals, IPS signatures and action, destinations and ports, access rules, sample URLs, user agents, file events To find out what your source is doing (1 to 240 minutes) get_recent_changes GET /v1/context/changes?hours=24 PseudoCo change calendar: ID, system, change, requester, time, implemented or scheduled Something broke at a specific time get_business_services GET /v1/context/services Services, criticality, business hours, owner, impact if down, what each depends on To turn a network finding into business impact and severity get_oncall GET /v1/context/oncall Who is on call and the wake-up policy To decide whether to wake someone get_saas_status GET /v1/context/saas-status Status of Webex, Microsoft 365, payments gateway, Salesforce To rule a provider outage in or out get_light_status GET /v1/status Your light: on or off, severity, summary, other open seats at your table Before clear_issue

docs.title: Action out
docs.text: Tool (MCP) REST Does Rules signal_issue POST /v1/signal {"severity","summary"} Lights your table's bulb in your color. Severity sets brightness; critical pulses Call when STATUS is issue. Calling again updates severity and summary clear_issue POST /v1/clear Turns your light off Only after verifying the fix, and only if your light is on stop_my_lane POST /v1/lane/stop Stops traffic from your watch source IP only Only after a human approves. Changes no shared configuration

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: What Where MCP (Streamable HTTP) Lab Tools MCP URL on your seat card, path /mcp OpenAPI 3.1 specs /openapi-light.json (Lab Actions, 6 operations), /openapi-context.json (Lab Context, 4 operations) Board /board

docs.title: Canvas cannot see Lab Tools
docs.text:
• Canvas → Integrations → Custom Integrations: is Lab Tools there, with Enabled for me ticked and your credential added? Add it with ⋯ → Replace my bearer token.
  • Start a new board after adding the credential; an open board may not pick it up.
  • A Studio MCP integration with Canvas Direct does not make tools appear in Canvas chat. Canvas uses its own Custom Integrations (OpenAPI). Use Lab Tools there.

docs.title: "missing or invalid bearer token" (401)
docs.text:
Your seat token was mistyped, has a trailing space, or belongs to an earlier session (tokens change between sessions). Copy it again from your seat card, then update the credential:

  • Canvas: Lab Tools card → ⋯ → Replace my bearer token.
  • Studio: Manage → Integrations → your Lab Tools → ⋯ → Update credential.

docs.title: "rate limit" (429)
docs.text: Your token made more than 30 calls in a minute, usually an agent stuck in a loop. Wait a minute and check the agent's instructions for a step it repeats.

docs.title: Studio discovers fewer than 10 tools
docs.text: Use ⋯ → Rediscover on the integration (it asks for your token again). If the URL is not the one on your seat card, edit the integration.

docs.title: My light will not turn off
docs.text: clear_issue only clears your seat. If another seat at your table still has an open issue, the bulb keeps cycling their color. Check get_light_status: it lists the other open seats at your table.

docs.title: The agent says my lane is stopped, but events continue
docs.text: Events reach Splunk a minute or two late. Wait two minutes and check again with a short window (minutes=5). If events still arrive, call stop_my_lane again (it is safe to repeat) and tell a proctor.

docs.title: Canvas shows "There is an issue connecting to this canvas"
docs.text: The chat reconnects by itself. If the answer seems to disappear, reload the page; finished answers are kept on the board.
